name: presubmit
description: Catches the common manuscript submission mistakes before a journal does. Checks sections, author/affiliation/email completeness, abstract length and keyword counts, reference problems (duplicates by DOI or text, missing years, malformed DOIs, citations with no matching reference, references never cited), missing ethics/disclosure statements, and deterministic language/typography errors. Also catches what an editorial round actually flags: placeholders and unresolved tracked changes or comments left in the submitted .docx, a declared word count over the format's limit, more references than the format allows, effect estimates reported without a confidence interval, trials named only by acronym, the same study described twice, and the authors' own ongoing study promoted in the conclusion. Reads .docx/.pdf/.tex/.txt, applies a journal profile (Cureus and Annals Ideas and Opinions built in), and prints a severity-ranked readiness report with fix hints. Offline and deterministic by default — no language model, no spell dictionary, so no false positives on medical terms; an opt-in --online flag additionally asks PubMed whether any cited paper has been corrected or retracted.
